title: Understanding Social Capital Theory
text:
Social capital refers to the resources embedded within social networks and relationships. It encompasses the value derived from an individual's connections, including trust, reciprocity, and mutual support within a community or group.

Unlike physical capital (machines) or human capital (skills), social capital is relational; it exists between people. Key components include 'bonding' capital—ties that bind similar groups together—and 'bridging' capital—ties that link different backgrounds and communities.
